<!-- snippet:one-percent-treaty-pitch -->

Your species spends {{< var global_military_spending_annual_2024 >}} a year on military forces. That amount is enough to buy enough bullets to murder every man, woman, and child on Earth {{< var bullets_per_person_annual_nounit >}} times. Every year. If every nation reduces that by 1% at the same time, the balance of power stays identical. No country gets weaker. Nobody loses a single war they would have otherwise won. You just become slightly less capable of destroying a planet you're still living on (which should be fine, since you were already capable of destroying it {{< var nuclear_winter_overkill_factor_nounit >}} times over).

That 1% is {{< var treaty_annual_funding >}} a year. For comparison, that's roughly what Americans spend on Valentine's Day. You are currently spending more on heart-shaped candy than on curing heart disease.

{{< var treaty_annual_funding_latex >}}

A 1% Treaty is a piece of paper that says every signatory nation redirects that 1% so any patient can join pragmatic clinical trials for the most promising treatments. That's it. That's the whole idea. On Wishonia, we fought for 12,000 years before we figured this out. Your species has been thinking it over for several thousand years, so you're actually ahead of schedule (barely).

<!-- /snippet:one-percent-treaty-pitch -->

## The Treaty

**THE TREATY FOR THE 1% REALLOCATION OF MILITARY EXPENDITURES TOWARDS BIOMEDICAL RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT FOR THE PREVENTION OF HUMAN SUFFERING AND DEATH**

*(Short title: the treaty where you buy 1% fewer bombs and, in exchange, stop dying of things)*

<!-- snippet:one-percent-treaty-text -->

WHEREAS, humanity pays governments \$36 trillion a year [@world-bank-government-expense-pct-gdp] for the service of promoting the general welfare, defined as the median health and wealth of the citizenry;

WHEREAS, the citizenry would like to actually receive this service at some point;

WHEREAS, they instead used {{< var cumulative_military_spending_fed_era >}} of their salary to murder approximately {{< var war_deaths_since_1900_nounit >}} humans [@lost-human-capital-war-cost] over the last century of their employment;

WHEREAS, these murdered humans included 930,000 physicians, 310,000 scientists, 620,000 engineers, 1.24 million nurses, 3.1 million teachers, and {{< var war_children_killed_since_1900_nounit >}} children who will never grow up to replace them [@lost-human-capital-war-cost];

WHEREAS, murdering {{< var war_deaths_since_1900_nounit >}} people is the opposite of promoting their welfare, and would be grounds for termination in any other service contract humans have ever signed;

WHEREAS, the governments of Earth have been hitting each other for roughly 10,000 years because the other one hit them last;

WHEREAS, this is the conflict resolution strategy of four-year-olds;

WHEREAS, four-year-olds eventually get tired and take a nap, and these governments have failed to apply naps to foreign policy;

WHEREAS, the governments of Earth possess nuclear weapons sufficient to end civilization {{< var nuclear_winter_overkill_factor_nounit >}} times but have not cured Alzheimer's once;

WHEREAS, global militaries would retain capacity for 121.2 apocalypses, which is functionally indistinguishable from {{< var nuclear_winter_overkill_factor_nounit >}} times over, because civilization only ends in whole numbers, and after the first apocalypse the remaining 121 are redundant;

WHEREAS, governments spend {{< var global_military_spending_annual_2024 >}} a year on their capacity for mass murder, which is enough to buy {{< var bullets_per_person_annual_nounit >}} bullets for every human alive every year, which is more bullets than any human has a reasonable use for;

WHEREAS, governments spend {{< var military_to_government_clinical_trials_spending_ratio_nounit >}} dollars on the capacity for orphan manufacturing for every one dollar spent on the trials that might cure what is actually going to kill their citizens;

WHEREAS, the United States Department of Defense has "misplaced" $2.46 trillion, failed seven consecutive audits trying to find it [@pentagon-unaccounted-2-5t], and then requested additional trillions without explanation or apology;

WHEREAS, the $27 billion this treaty requests is smaller than a rounding error on the $2.46 trillion the Pentagon has already "misplaced";

WHEREAS, politicians are coin-operated, and the coin is currently supplied by the manufacturers of the things that kill the politicians' constituents, which is a loop that converts good intentions into missiles automatically, and the signatories propose not to ask the politicians to become better people (which is clearly out of the question) but to replace the coin;

WHEREAS, the United States spent {{< var us_military_spending_1939_annual_2024usd >}} a year on its military in 1939, in today's dollars. It won World War II. Then it cut military spending by {{< var post_ww2_military_cut_pct >}} in two years [@us-post-wwii-military-spending-cut] and produced the biggest economic boom in history. Today it spends {{< var us_military_spending_current_vs_prewar_multiplier_nounit >}} times the 1939 figure, in peacetime [@us-military-spending-historical-constant-dollars]. Therefore, unless the human genome has significantly degraded in the two generations since, a one percent reallocation should be manageable;

WHEREAS, without the cumulative losses from war and disease the average human would earn {{< var war_counterfactual_gdp_per_capita >}} a year instead of {{< var global_avg_income_2025 >}} [@lost-human-capital-war-cost]. Every citizen pays twice. Once in taxes that built the weapons. Again, every year, in wages they do not earn, because the scientists and engineers and builders who would have made the world richer were killed before they could;

WHEREAS, global military spending has been growing {{< var global_military_spending_real_cagr_20yr >}} a year, in real terms, for twenty years [@sipri-milex-2024]. If it keeps growing, every human alive today will be billed about {{< var global_war_cost_lifetime_per_person_baseline >}} over the rest of their life to pay for it [@1-pct-treaty-impact-paper-2025]. Some of that arrives as taxes. Some as wages they never earn. Some as buildings that get bombed and rebuilt. Most of the money will buy explosions in countries they cannot find on a map;

WHEREAS, cutting one percent now, and making it stick, flattens that growth. That saves the average person about {{< var peace_dividend_lifetime_per_person >}} over their lifetime, in taxes they do not pay, wages they do earn, and valuable humans and buildings that do not get exploded;

WHEREAS, diseases kill more people than all wars combined [@pandemics-vs-wars] and, unlike wars, do not even have the decency to be quick about it;

WHEREAS, your chance of dying in a terrorist attack is approximately 1 in {{< var annual_terrorism_death_risk_denominator_nounit >}}, and your chance of dying of a disease is 100%, and your current budget does not reflect this;

WHEREAS, only 15 diseases get their first effective treatment each year [@diseases-getting-first-treatment-annually], while {{< var diseases_without_effective_treatment >}} are still waiting, forming a queue to not die longer than any queue humans have ever voluntarily stood in;

WHEREAS, there are {{< var safe_compounds_count >}} known safe compounds, and {{< var unexplored_ratio >}} of their potential uses have never been tested on any human;

WHEREAS, pragmatic clinical trials built into ordinary healthcare cost {{< var dfda_pragmatic_trial_cost_per_patient >}} per patient, instead of the usual {{< var traditional_phase3_cost_per_patient >}}. That makes trials {{< var dfda_trial_cost_reduction_factor >}} cheaper. It lets {{< var dfda_trial_capacity_multiplier >}} times as many people join. The wait to test treatments for every known disease drops from {{< var status_quo_queue_clearance_years >}} to {{< var dfda_queue_clearance_years >}};

WHEREAS, at that expanded capacity, treatments that would have sat undiscovered for centuries arrive {{< var dfda_trial_capacity_treatment_acceleration_years_nounit >}} years sooner on average;

WHEREAS, discovering treatments centuries sooner is projected to prevent approximately {{< var dfda_trial_capacity_plus_efficacy_lag_lives_saved >}} and {{< var dfda_trial_capacity_plus_efficacy_lag_suffering_hours >}} of human suffering [@1-pct-treaty-impact-paper-2025], which are not metaphors and refer to specific future humans with specific future plans for next Tuesday;

WHEREAS, every signatory to this Treaty will personally be dead within 80 years, which is mentioned not to be rude but because you seem weirdly calm about this;

WHEREAS, someone you love is, at this moment, suffering from a disease;

WHEREAS, the treatment that would help them exists as an untested compound on a shelf, because the money that would have tested it was busy turning into a missile;

WHEREAS, that missile incinerated a child who could have grown up to discover the cure;

WHEREAS, you lose the treatment, you lose the scientist, you get the inflation, you get the tax bill, you get to pay for her murder;

NOW, THEREFORE, the undersigned nations agree to try a different approach, as follows:

**Article I**: Each signatory shall redirect exactly 1% of its annual military budget to **the 1% Treaty Fund**, split as follows: {{< var dih_treasury_medical_research_pct >}} to pragmatic clinical trials; {{< var victory_bond_funding_pct >}} to perpetual returns on [Incentive Alignment Bonds](incentive-alignment-bonds.qmd) [@iab-paper-2025]; and {{< var iab_political_incentive_funding_pct >}} to a Political Incentive Fund that supports campaigns of legislators who vote to implement and expand this Treaty, structured in each signatory nation according to its domestic campaign finance and public-official-compensation laws.

**Article II**: Transfers shall be automatic, immediate, and irrevocable. The money moves on the first of every month, the way your mortgage does, except nobody has to call and yell at anyone.

**Article III**: The percentage can go up. It never goes down. When the treaty works, a mandatory review raises it. Article I is written in percentages, not dollars, so when the treaty grows, the bondholder payouts grow and the Political Incentive Fund grows. The people being paid will want the treaty to keep growing. They will keep wanting this until war and disease stop killing people. Then they can stop.

Compliance shall be enforced by [Incentive Alignment Bonds](incentive-alignment-bonds.qmd) [@iab-paper-2025]. The Political Incentive Fund shall reward legislators according to their recorded votes on this Treaty: campaign support for those seeking reelection, post-office appointments for those retiring. No funds shall pass directly to any legislator; all disbursements shall route through a scoring algorithm, which is apparently the only legal way to train a senator. The signatories note that the NRA already perfected this technology, and that this Treaty plagiarizes it, substituting "not dying from diseases" for "guns."

**Article IV**: Compliance shall be verified by public ledger and independent audits. Relabeling a submarine as "humanitarian infrastructure" will be noticed, because submarines are large and loud and do not fit in the humanitarian infrastructure drawer.

**Article V**: Non-compliant parties shall be given a stern talking to, and their compliant political opponents shall be funded to the full extent of the law via the Political Incentive Fund established in Article III.

**Article VI**: Citizens can sue their own government in their own courts if it stops paying.

**Article VII**: Bondholders of Incentive Alignment Bonds issued under Article I shall have direct standing to sue any signatory government in its own courts for non-payment, in addition to the citizen standing granted by Article VI. Unlike citizens, bondholders arrive pre-equipped with lawyers.

**Article VIII**: Withdrawal requires unanimous consent of all parties plus 10-year notice. Your country would need every other signatory to agree, which requires a decade of phone calls none of them are going to return.

**Article IX**: This treaty supersedes all conflicting domestic law. Including the subsection your legislature added at 2 a.m. last session specifically to make sure this couldn't happen.

**Article X**: Entry into force upon signature by two states. Two signatures. That's the bar. Your species once got 193 countries to agree that chemical weapons were bad. This asks for 2.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the undersigned, being of sound mind (debatable) and tired of watching their loved ones die of preventable diseases, have executed this Treaty on behalf of populations who would have executed it much sooner if anyone had asked them, and on behalf of someone each signatory can picture right now who is currently dying of a disease that the money in Article I will help test a cure for.

<!-- /snippet:one-percent-treaty-text -->
